content.text: All elements sit at or above the preferred position: Customer has an unconditional without-cause right on 30 days' notice with prepaid-fee refund, and no Vendor convenience right exists anywhere in the document.

input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 gives us an unconditional right to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form without cause, and Section 29.4 fixes that notice period at thirty days — at our preferred 30-day threshold. Section 9.4 (reinforced by Section 10.2) requires Vendor to refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination, i.e. a pro-rata refund, and no early-termination fee or penalty appears anywhere in the document. Vendor has no convenience or without-cause termination right: its termination rights are limited to mutual material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and the narrow IP-remedy carve-out in 20.5/Section 20 (which expressly bars terminating unaffected Services). The three-year term in Section 8.1 is therefore fully exitable by us on 30 days' notice. Customer's thirty-day non-renewal notice in Section 8.2 is a renewal mechanic, not a Vendor convenience right, and is not flagged here. Preferred position met; no redline.
